title: Hereditary discrepancy and factorization norms (AimPL) — Open problems

problems.sourceStatement: There is a universal constant $c>0$ s.t. for every $v_1,v_2,...,v_n \in \mathbb{B_2}^d$, there exist signs $\epsilon_1,...,\epsilon_n\in \{-1,1\}$ s.t. $|| \sum_{i=1}^n \epsilon_i v_i||_{\infty} \le c$
problems.problem: Prove the Komlós conjecture: for any multiset of $n$ vectors in the Euclidean unit ball of $\mathbb{R}^d$, there exist $\pm 1$ signs whose signed sum has $\ell_\infty$ norm bounded by an absolute constant, independent of both the dimension $d$ and the number of vectors $n$. Equivalently, the vector-balancing constant $\mathrm{vb}(B_2^d, B_\infty^d)$ is bounded uniformly in $d$. Proved in September 2026 by Guo, Fang and Lu (arXiv:2609.11189) with the explicit constant $3\sqrt{2\pi}$; the proof is existential.
problems.wordDescription: The Komlós conjecture was for decades one of the central open problems in combinatorial discrepancy; it was proved in September 2026 (see below). It asserts that vectors of Euclidean norm at most one can always be signed so that every coordinate of the signed sum stays within an absolute constant, no matter how many vectors there are or how high the dimension is. It strictly generalizes the Beck-Fiala conjecture (scale each element's incidence vector by $1/\sqrt{t}$), and in the special case of normalized $\pm 1$ vectors it recovers Spencer's theorem. For decades the best general bound was Banaszczyk's $O(\sqrt{\log n})$ (1998), sharpened to $O(\sqrt{\log \min\{d, n\}})$ via the Gaussian slice estimates of Barthe, Guédon, Mendelson and Naor (2005). In 2025 Bansal and Jiang broke this barrier with an algorithmic $\widetilde{O}(\log^{1/4} n)$ bound. The conjecture is known to hold in a smoothed-analysis model (Bansal, Jiang, Meka, Singla and Sinha, 2022: Gaussian perturbations of $n = \omega(d\log d)$ vectors), and for all $t$-sparse $0/1$ instances with $t \geq (\log n)^{1+o(1)}$ via the Beck-Fiala results of Bansal-Jiang and Altschuler-Tikhomirov (see Problem 1.15), and these were the strongest results until September 2026, when Guo, Fang and Lu (arXiv:2609.11189) proved the conjecture in full generality: every finite family of vectors in $B_2^d$ admits a signing with $\ell_\infty$-norm less than $3\sqrt{2\pi} \approx 7.52$, independently of $d$ and $n$. Their argument is an open-set version of Banaszczyk's convex-body transform in which the transformed body is shown to support a probability density whose directional total variation stays bounded by a fixed $\kappa$ in every direction (with $\kappa\|v\|_2 \leq 1/3$), allowing a sign for every input vector to be recovered. The proof is existential (no polynomial-time algorithm is given, see Problem 1.1), the constant is not claimed to be optimal, and the best lower bound on the constant is $1 + \sqrt{2}$ (Kunisky 2023).
problems.mathematicalConditions: Setting. For integers $d, n \geq 1$ and vectors $v_1, \dots, v_n \in \mathbb{R}^d$ with $\|v_i\|_2 \leq 1$, let $\mathrm{disc}_\infty(v_1, \dots, v_n) = \min_{\epsilon \in \{-1,1\}^n} \left\|\sum_{i=1}^n \epsilon_i v_i\right\|_\infty$, and let $K(d, n)$ be the supremum of this quantity over all such families; set $K = \sup_{d, n} K(d, n)$. Conjecture (Komlós). $K < \infty$; i.e. there is an absolute constant $c$ with $K(d, n) \leq c$ for all $d, n$. Benchmarks. Lower bound: $K \geq 1 + \sqrt{2} - o(1)$, via explicit matrices with unit-norm columns and discrepancy approaching $1 + \sqrt{2}$ (Kunisky 2023). Upper bounds: $K(d, n) = O(\sqrt{\log \min\{d, n\}})$ (Banaszczyk 1998 with Barthe-Guédon-Mendelson-Naor 2005), and $K(d, n) = \widetilde{O}(\log^{1/4} n)$ where $\widetilde{O}$ hides $\mathrm{poly}(\log\log n)$ factors (Bansal-Jiang 2025, algorithmic). In the smoothed model where each $v_i$ is replaced by $v_i + g_i$ with $g_i \sim N(0, \sigma^2 I_d/d)$ i.i.d. and fixed $\sigma > 0$, the bound $O(1)$ holds with high probability whenever $n = \omega(d \log d)$ (Bansal-Jiang-Meka-Singla-Sinha 2022). Complete resolution. Either (A) a proof that $K \leq c$ for some explicit or non-explicit absolute constant $c$, or (B) a disproof: a sequence of families $(v^{(j)}_1, \dots, v^{(j)}_{n_j}) \subset B_2^{d_j}$ with $\mathrm{disc}_\infty \to \infty$. Minimal progress that counts as a solution of this record. Any one of: (i) an upper bound $K(d, n) = O((\log n)^{\gamma})$ (or $O((\log \min\{d,n\})^{\gamma})$) for some constant $\gamma < 1/4$; (ii) a bound $K(d, n) = O(1)$ valid for all $n$ and $d$ in an infinite parameter regime that is not implied by the Beck-Fiala results (e.g. all $n \leq d^{C}$ for a constant $C \geq 1$, or all $n \geq C d \log d$ without perturbation); (iii) a super-constant lower bound, $K(d, n) \to \infty$ along any sequence $(d, n)$; (iv) the smoothed statement for $n = O(d \log d)$ with perturbation magnitude $\sigma$ allowed to depend polynomially on $1/d$ or $1/n$, or a proof of the conjecture for a natural non-smoothed random model of vectors in $B_2^d$ for all $n \geq d$. Purely improving the $\mathrm{poly}(\log\log n)$ factor hidden in $\widetilde{O}(\log^{1/4} n)$, or the constant in an existing bound, does not count. Resolution (September 2026). Guo, Fang and Lu (arXiv:2609.11189, Theorem 1.1) prove that for all $m, n \geq 1$ and all $v_1, \dots, v_n \in \mathbb{R}^m$ with $\|v_j\|_2 \leq 1$ there exist $\epsilon \in \{-1,1\}^n$ with $\|\sum_{j} \epsilon_j v_j\|_\infty < 3\sqrt{2\pi}$; i.e. $K \leq 3\sqrt{2\pi}$. This is alternative (A) of the complete-resolution criterion, so the record is solved. Not part of this record: the optimal constant ($1 + \sqrt{2} \leq K \leq 3\sqrt{2\pi}$) and a polynomial-time algorithm achieving $O(1)$ (Problem 1.1).

literature.title: J. Komlós, A generalization of a problem of Steinhaus, Acta Mathematica Academiae Scientiarum Hungaricae 18:217-229, 1967
literature.description: Komlós's paper on signed sums of vectors, generalizing a problem of Steinhaus; the Komlós conjecture is traditionally attributed to Komlós and appears in print in Spencer's 'Ten lectures on the probabilistic method' (1987).

literature.title: J. Spencer, Six standard deviations suffice, Transactions of the American Mathematical Society 289(2):679-706, 1985
literature.description: Proves $\mathrm{disc} = O(\sqrt{n})$ for $n$ sets on $n$ elements and, more generally, $O(\sqrt{n \log(2m/n)})$ for $m \geq n$ sets; the Komlós conjecture is the vector generalization of this theorem.

literature.title: W. Banaszczyk, Balancing vectors and Gaussian measures of n-dimensional convex bodies, Random Structures & Algorithms 12(4):351-360, 1998
literature.description: Proves the vector-balancing theorem for convex bodies of Gaussian measure at least $1/2$; applied to a scaled $\ell_\infty$ ball it gives $O(\sqrt{\log n})$ for the Komlós problem and $O(\sqrt{k \log n})$ for degree-$k$ set systems.

literature.title: F. Barthe, O. Guédon, S. Mendelson, A. Naor, A probabilistic approach to the geometry of the $\ell_p^n$-ball, Annals of Probability 33(2):480-513, 2005
literature.description: The '[Naor'05]' reference of the AimPL page. Gaussian-measure estimates for slices of the $\ell_\infty^n$ ball that, combined with Banaszczyk's theorem, give the Komlós bound $O(\sqrt{\log d})$ where $d$ is the dimension of the span of the vectors.

literature.title: N. Bansal, H. Jiang, Decoupling via affine spectral-independence: Beck-Fiala and Komlós bounds beyond Banaszczyk, arXiv:2508.03961, 2025
literature.description: Gives an algorithmic $\widetilde{O}(\log^{1/4} n)$ bound for the Komlós problem, the first improvement over Banaszczyk's $O(\sqrt{\log n})$, and proves the Beck-Fiala conjecture (discrepancy $O(\sqrt{k})$) for all degrees $k \geq \log^2 n$, together with an $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{k} + \sqrt{\log n})$ bound for every $k$.

literature.title: N. Bansal, H. Jiang, R. Meka, S. Singla, M. Sinha, Smoothed analysis of the Komlós conjecture, ICALP 2022; arXiv:2204.11427
literature.description: Proves the Komlós conjecture in a smoothed-analysis model: if $n = \omega(d \log d)$ arbitrary vectors in the unit ball are perturbed by small Gaussian noise, then with high probability there is a signing of $\ell_\infty$ discrepancy $O(1)$ (they also show $n = \omega(d\log d)$ is essentially necessary for this smoothed statement).

literature.title: D. J. Altschuler, K. Tikhomirov, Online Beck-Fiala down to logarithmic sparsity, arXiv:2607.14238, 2026
literature.description: Proves the Beck-Fiala conjecture (and hence the $0/1$ sparse case of Komlós) for degree $d \geq (\log T)^{1+o(1)}$ via an efficient online prefix-discrepancy algorithm; see Problem 1.15.

literature.title: D. Kunisky, The discrepancy of unsatisfiable matrices and a lower bound for the Komlós conjecture constant, SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics 37(2):586-603, 2023
literature.description: Explicit matrices with unit $\ell_2$-norm columns and discrepancy approaching $1 + \sqrt{2} \approx 2.414$, built from clause-variable matrices of unsatisfiable formulas; the best known lower bound on the Komlós constant $K$.

literature.title: S. Guo, E. X. Fang, J. Lu, Vector balancing via directional total variation, arXiv:2609.11189, 2026
literature.description: Proof of the Komlós conjecture with constant $3\sqrt{2\pi}$ (Theorem 1.1): every finite family of vectors of Euclidean norm at most one has a signing of $\ell_\infty$-norm less than $3\sqrt{2\pi}$, independently of dimension and size. Method: an open-set Banaszczyk transform preserving a directional-total-variation bound $\kappa$ on a supporting density when $\kappa\|v\|_2 \leq 1/3$. Existential; no polynomial-time algorithm; constant not claimed optimal. Corollary 1.2 gives the Beck-Fiala bound $3\sqrt{2\pi t}$.

problems.verificationNotes: Re-verified on 2026-09-20 against http://aimpl.org/hereddiscrep/1/, the arXiv listings of the cited papers and the 2026 survey arXiv:2608.00140. Status set to solved on 2026-09-20 on the basis of arXiv:2609.11189 (Guo, Fang and Lu, submitted 10 September 2026); Theorem 1.1 ($K \leq 3\sqrt{2\pi}$) and Corollary 1.2 ($\mathrm{disc} < 3\sqrt{2\pi t}$ for column sparsity $t$) were checked against the full text, which states that the argument is existential and that the constant is not claimed to be optimal. The paper is a preprint. The lower bound $1 + \sqrt{2}$ was checked against arXiv:2111.02974 (Kunisky, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 2023).
problems.statusDetails: Solved (existentially) in September 2026: Guo, Fang and Lu (arXiv:2609.11189, Theorem 1.1) prove $K \leq 3\sqrt{2\pi} \approx 7.52$ for all $d$ and $n$, via an open-set Banaszczyk transform controlled by directional total variation of densities. Earlier bounds: $c = O(\sqrt{\log \min\{d, n\}})$ (Banaszczyk 1998 with Barthe-Guédon-Mendelson-Naor 2005), $\widetilde{O}(\log^{1/4} n)$ with a polynomial-time algorithm (Bansal-Jiang, arXiv:2508.03961, 2025), and the smoothed-analysis case $n = \omega(d \log d)$ (Bansal-Jiang-Meka-Singla-Sinha, arXiv:2204.11427, 2022). The lower bound on the constant is $1 + \sqrt{2}$ (Kunisky 2023). Open follow-ups: the exact constant, and a polynomial-time algorithm achieving $O(1)$ (Problem 1.1), since the Guo-Fang-Lu argument is non-constructive.

problems.sourceStatement: Find a polynomial time algorithm to find the signs above.
problems.problem: Design a polynomial-time algorithm that, given vectors $v_1, \dots, v_n$ in the Euclidean unit ball of $\mathbb{R}^d$, finds signs $\epsilon_i \in \{-1, 1\}$ achieving the strongest known (Komlós-type) discrepancy guarantee on $\|\sum_i \epsilon_i v_i\|_\infty$.
problems.wordDescription: Banaszczyk's bound $O(\sqrt{\log \min\{d, n\}})$ for the Komlós problem was originally non-constructive, and finding the signs efficiently was a major challenge. The workshop-era status was a constructive $O(\log \min\{d, n\})$ bound via the partial-coloring algorithms of Bansal and of Lovett-Meka and the convex-geometric algorithm of Rothvoss. Shortly after the workshop the gap was closed: Bansal, Dadush and Garg (FOCS 2016) gave a polynomial-time algorithm matching Banaszczyk's bound, Bansal, Dadush, Garg and Lovett made the full Banaszczyk vector-balancing theorem constructive (the Gram-Schmidt walk), and Dadush, Garg, Lovett and Nikolov gave an alternative multiplicative-weight-update approach. Since then every improvement of the existential bound has been algorithmic as well: the current best general bound $\widetilde{O}(\log^{1/4} n)$ of Bansal and Jiang (2025) is achieved by a polynomial-time algorithm. Until September 2026 the problem was therefore resolved relative to the state of Problem 1.05. The situation changed with Guo, Fang and Lu (arXiv:2609.11189), who proved the Komlós conjecture existentially with constant $3\sqrt{2\pi}$: their recursive open-set Banaszczyk transform, its membership queries and the resulting sign recovery are not known to be implementable in polynomial time, so the constructive problem is now a genuine open question. The gap is between the best algorithmic guarantee $\widetilde{O}(\log^{1/4} n)$ and the existential $O(1)$.
problems.mathematicalConditions: Setting. Let $f^{*}(d, n)$ denote the best bound currently proven for Problem 1.05, i.e. the smallest known function with $K(d, n) \leq f^{*}(d, n)$; since Guo-Fang-Lu (arXiv:2609.11189, 2026), $f^{*}(d, n) = 3\sqrt{2\pi}$, an absolute constant. Problem. Give an algorithm that, on input $v_1, \dots, v_n \in \mathbb{R}^d$ with $\|v_i\|_2 \leq 1$ (rational entries), runs in time $\mathrm{poly}(n, d, \text{bit-size})$ and outputs $\epsilon \in \{-1, 1\}^n$ with $\left\|\sum_{i=1}^n \epsilon_i v_i\right\|_\infty \leq C\, f^{*}(d, n)$ for an absolute constant $C$ (randomized algorithms succeeding with probability $\geq 2/3$ are allowed). Benchmarks. Constructive $O(\log \min\{d,n\})$ (Bansal 2010; Lovett-Meka 2012; Rothvoss 2014); constructive $O(\sqrt{\log \min\{d, n\}})$ (Bansal-Dadush-Garg 2016; Bansal-Dadush-Garg-Lovett 2018; Dadush-Garg-Lovett-Nikolov 2019); constructive $\widetilde{O}(\log^{1/4} n)$ (Bansal-Jiang 2025). Existential: $K \leq 3\sqrt{2\pi}$ (Guo-Fang-Lu 2026, non-constructive). Hence the constructive and existential states no longer coincide: the gap is $\widetilde{O}(\log^{1/4} n)$ (algorithmic) versus $O(1)$ (existential). Complete resolution. A polynomial-time algorithm achieving $\|\sum_i \epsilon_i v_i\|_\infty \leq c$ for an absolute constant $c$ (matching the existential bound of Guo-Fang-Lu up to constants). Minimal progress that counts as a solution of this record. Any of: (i) a polynomial-time algorithm whose guarantee is $O((\log n)^\gamma)$ with $\gamma < 1/4$ (any $o(\log^{1/4} n)$ guarantee, since the existential bound is $O(1)$); (ii) a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm matching a bound of $O(\sqrt{\log \min\{d,n\}})$ or better; (iii) a near-linear-time (e.g. $\widetilde{O}(nd)$) algorithm matching $O(\sqrt{\log \min\{d,n\}})$; (iv) an efficient algorithm that, given any input, either certifies (via a polynomial-time verifiable certificate) that its discrepancy is at least a constant times its output, or achieves $O(1)$; (v) a polynomial-time, or even subexponential-time ($2^{o(n)}\,\mathrm{poly}(d)$), randomized implementation of the Guo-Fang-Lu argument (the recursive open-set transform and its sign recovery), or a polynomial-time algorithm achieving $O(\sqrt{t})$ for all $t$-sparse $0/1$ inputs with $t \leq \log n$ (the constructive Beck-Fiala conjecture, Problem 1.15).

literature.title: N. Bansal, Constructive algorithms for discrepancy minimization, FOCS 2010
literature.description: The SDP-based random-walk algorithm that first made classical discrepancy bounds (Spencer's theorem and $O(\sqrt{t}\log n)$ for $t$-sparse systems) constructive.

literature.title: S. Lovett, R. Meka, Constructive discrepancy minimization by walking on the edges, FOCS 2012; SIAM Journal on Computing 44(5):1573-1582, 2015
literature.description: Simpler 'edge-walk' algorithm for partial colorings, matching Spencer's theorem and giving constructive $O(\log \min\{d,n\})$-type bounds for the Komlós problem.

literature.title: T. Rothvoss, Constructive discrepancy minimization for convex sets, FOCS 2014; SIAM Journal on Computing 46(1):224-234, 2017
literature.description: Convex-geometric partial-coloring algorithm (Gaussian projection onto a convex body) that makes all Gaussian-measure based partial-coloring bounds constructive.

literature.title: N. Bansal, D. Dadush, S. Garg, An algorithm for Komlós conjecture matching Banaszczyk's bound, FOCS 2016; SIAM Journal on Computing 48(2):534-553, 2019
literature.description: First polynomial-time algorithm achieving Banaszczyk's $O(\sqrt{\log \min\{d, n\}})$ bound for the Komlós problem (and $O(\sqrt{t \log n})$ for Beck-Fiala).

literature.title: N. Bansal, D. Dadush, S. Garg, S. Lovett, The Gram-Schmidt walk: a cure for the Banaszczyk blues, STOC 2018; Theory of Computing 15(21):1-27, 2019
literature.description: Constructive version of Banaszczyk's full vector-balancing theorem (for arbitrary convex bodies of Gaussian measure at least $1/2$), via the Gram-Schmidt walk.

literature.title: D. Dadush, S. Garg, S. Lovett, A. Nikolov, Towards a constructive version of Banaszczyk's vector balancing theorem, APPROX/RANDOM 2016; Theory of Computing 15(15):1-58, 2019
literature.description: Multiplicative-weight-update based algorithm for Banaszczyk's theorem given a suitable subgaussian distribution; also discusses the tightness of the Gaussian-measure threshold $1/2$.

literature.title: N. Bansal, H. Jiang, Decoupling via affine spectral-independence: Beck-Fiala and Komlós bounds beyond Banaszczyk, arXiv:2508.03961, 2025
literature.description: Gives an algorithmic $\widetilde{O}(\log^{1/4} n)$ bound for the Komlós problem, the first improvement over Banaszczyk's $O(\sqrt{\log n})$, and proves the Beck-Fiala conjecture (discrepancy $O(\sqrt{k})$) for all degrees $k \geq \log^2 n$, together with an $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{k} + \sqrt{\log n})$ bound for every $k$.

literature.title: S. Guo, E. X. Fang, J. Lu, Vector balancing via directional total variation, arXiv:2609.11189, 2026
literature.description: Existential proof of the Komlós conjecture ($\|\sum_i \epsilon_i v_i\|_\infty < 3\sqrt{2\pi}$). The authors state that no polynomial-time implementation of the recursive domain construction, its membership queries and the sign recovery is established; making this bound algorithmic is now the content of this problem.

problems.statusDetails: Open as of September 2026. A polynomial-time algorithm matching Banaszczyk's $O(\sqrt{\log \min\{d, n\}})$ bound was given by Bansal, Dadush and Garg (FOCS 2016); constructive versions of the full Banaszczyk theorem followed (Gram-Schmidt walk, STOC 2018; Dadush-Garg-Lovett-Nikolov). The best algorithmic bound is $\widetilde{O}(\log^{1/4} n)$ (Bansal-Jiang, arXiv:2508.03961, 2025). The existential bound is now $O(1)$: Guo, Fang and Lu (arXiv:2609.11189, 2026) prove $\|\sum_i \epsilon_i v_i\|_\infty < 3\sqrt{2\pi}$ for every input, but their proof is non-constructive and no polynomial-time implementation is known. The constructive problem is therefore no longer equivalent to Problem 1.05; it asks for an efficient algorithm closing the $\widetilde{O}(\log^{1/4} n)$ versus $O(1)$ gap.

problems.sourceStatement: Given a set system $(V,\mathcal{S})$ with $V=[n]$, $\mathcal{S}=S_1,...,S_m$. Each $i\in V$ occurs in at most $t$ sets from $\mathcal{S}$. Then there is a coloring to the elements of $V$ achieving a discrepancy of $O(\sqrt{t})$. Komlós conjecture implies this by treating the incidence vector of each $i\in V$ as a vector and scaling it down by $\sqrt{t}$.
problems.problem: Prove the Beck-Fiala conjecture: every set system in which each element belongs to at most $t$ sets has a 2-coloring of discrepancy $O(\sqrt{t})$, with the bound independent of the number of elements $n$ and sets $m$. A constructive (polynomial-time) version is also sought. Proved in September 2026 by Guo, Fang and Lu (arXiv:2609.11189, Corollary 1.2): $\mathrm{disc} < 3\sqrt{2\pi t}$ for every $t \geq 1$ and all $n, m$, existentially. Algorithmically the conjecture is known for $t \geq (\log n)^{1+o(1)}$; a polynomial-time $O(\sqrt{t})$ algorithm for $t \leq \log n$ remains open.
problems.wordDescription: The Beck-Fiala conjecture (1981) is the sparse-set-system analogue of Spencer's theorem: if every element lies in at most $t$ sets, the discrepancy should be $O(\sqrt{t})$ rather than the $2t-1$ given by Beck and Fiala's iterated-rounding argument. For 35 years the only $n$-independent improvements were of the form $2t - o(t)$ (Bednarchak-Helm, Helm, Bukh: $2t - \log^{*} t$), while bounds with a mild dependence on $n$ came from Banaszczyk ($O(\sqrt{t \log n})$) and Spencer-type partial coloring ($O(\sqrt{t}\log n)$). In 2025 Bansal and Jiang introduced a decoupling technique via affine spectral independence and proved the conjecture for all $t \geq \log^2 n$ (after an $O(\sqrt{t \log\log n})$ bound for $t \geq \log^5 n$), together with an $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{t} + \sqrt{\log n})$ bound for every $t$. In 2026 Altschuler and Tikhomirov extended the conjecture's validity to $t \geq (\log n)^{1+o(1)}$ using an efficient online algorithm that controls all prefix discrepancies; their result is essentially optimal for online prefix discrepancy, which is $\omega(\sqrt{t})$ when $t = o(\log n)$, so pushing below the logarithmic threshold requires genuinely offline arguments. All of these results are algorithmic. In September 2026 Guo, Fang and Lu (arXiv:2609.11189) proved the Komlós conjecture with constant $3\sqrt{2\pi}$ and hence, by scaling each element's incidence vector by $1/\sqrt{t}$ (their Corollary 1.2), the Beck-Fiala conjecture itself: every set system of column sparsity $t$ has discrepancy less than $3\sqrt{2\pi t}$, for every $t \geq 1$ and independently of $n$ and $m$. The proof is existential, so the constructive version below the logarithmic sparsity threshold remains open, as does the optimal constant.
problems.mathematicalConditions: Setting. For a set system given by an incidence matrix $A \in \{0,1\}^{m \times n}$ (rows = sets, columns = elements) with at most $t$ ones in every column, let $\mathrm{disc}(A) = \min_{x \in \{-1,1\}^n} \|Ax\|_\infty$. Define $\mathrm{BF}(t) = \sup\{\mathrm{disc}(A)\}$ over all $m, n$ and all such $A$, and $\mathrm{BF}(t, n) = \sup$ over all such $A$ with $n$ columns (any $m$). Conjecture (Beck-Fiala). $\mathrm{BF}(t) = O(\sqrt{t})$. Benchmarks. Lower bound $\mathrm{BF}(t) = \Omega(\sqrt{t})$ (e.g. Hadamard-type systems on $n = m = t$). Upper bounds independent of $n$: $\mathrm{BF}(t) \leq 2t - 1$ (Beck-Fiala 1981), $\leq 2t - 3$ (Bednarchak-Helm 1997), $\leq 2t - \log^{*} t$ (Bukh 2016); $\mathrm{BF}(t) < 3\sqrt{2\pi t}$ for all $t \geq 1$ (Guo-Fang-Lu 2026, Corollary 1.2, from the Komlós bound $3\sqrt{2\pi}$; existential). Bounds depending on $n$: $\mathrm{BF}(t, n) = O(\sqrt{t \log n})$ (Banaszczyk 1998, algorithmic by Bansal-Dadush-Garg 2016); $\mathrm{BF}(t, n) = \widetilde{O}(\sqrt{t} + \sqrt{\log n})$ for all $t$ and $\mathrm{BF}(t, n) = O(\sqrt{t})$ for $t \geq \log^2 n$ (Bansal-Jiang 2025); $\mathrm{BF}(t, n) = O(\sqrt{t})$ for $t \geq (\log n)^{1 + \eta}$ for every fixed $\eta > 0$, via an online algorithm bounding all prefix discrepancies $\max_{k} \|A_{[k]} x_{[k]}\|_\infty$ (Altschuler-Tikhomirov 2026). Online prefix discrepancy is $\omega(\sqrt{t})$ when $t = o(\log n)$, so this threshold is optimal for online methods. All listed $n$-dependent upper bounds are attained by polynomial-time algorithms; the Guo-Fang-Lu bound is not known to be. Complete resolution. (A) a proof that $\mathrm{BF}(t) \leq C\sqrt{t}$ for an absolute constant $C$ and all $t$, or (B) a disproof: a sequence of systems with column sparsity $t_j$ and $\mathrm{disc} / \sqrt{t_j} \to \infty$. Either settles the record; an algorithmic proof additionally settles the constructive part. Minimal progress that counts as a solution of this record. Any of: (i) $\mathrm{BF}(t, n) = O(\sqrt{t})$ for all $t \geq C \log n$ (or any threshold $t \geq g(n)$ with $g(n) = O(\log n)$), i.e. reaching the logarithmic barrier offline; (ii) an $n$-independent bound $\mathrm{BF}(t) \leq (2 - \delta) t$ for a fixed $\delta > 0$ and all large $t$, or $\mathrm{BF}(t) = O(t^{1 - \delta})$; (iii) a uniform bound $\mathrm{BF}(t, n) \leq C\sqrt{t} + o(\sqrt{\log n})$ valid for all $t \leq \log n$ (improving the $\sqrt{\log n}$ term of Bansal-Jiang by more than $\mathrm{poly}(\log\log n)$ factors); (iv) for fixed $t \geq 3$, determining $\mathrm{BF}(t)$ exactly or improving the best known value of $\mathrm{BF}(t)$ by an additive constant that grows with $t$. Improving only the $\mathrm{poly}(\log\log n)$ factors in $\widetilde{O}$, or the $o(1)$ in $(\log n)^{1+o(1)}$, or constants in existing bounds, does not count. Resolution (September 2026). Guo, Fang and Lu establish (A) with $C = 3\sqrt{2\pi}$, so the record is solved. Not covered: the constructive part (a polynomial-time algorithm achieving $O(\sqrt{t})$ for $t \leq \log n$; see Problem 1.1 for the Komlós normalization) and the optimal constant in $\Omega(\sqrt{t}) \leq \mathrm{BF}(t) < 3\sqrt{2\pi t}$.

literature.title: J. Beck, T. Fiala, 'Integer-making' theorems, Discrete Applied Mathematics 3(1):1-8, 1981
literature.description: Introduces the problem and proves $\mathrm{disc} \leq 2t - 1$ by iterated rounding of a fractional coloring (linear-algebraic argument). Source of the conjecture $O(\sqrt{t})$.

literature.title: D. Bednarchak, M. Helm, A note on the Beck-Fiala theorem, Combinatorica 17(1):147-149, 1997
literature.description: Improves the Beck-Fiala bound to $2t - 3$ for $t \geq 3$.

literature.title: M. Helm, On the Beck-Fiala theorem, Discrete Mathematics 207(1-3):73-87, 1999
literature.description: Further additive-constant improvements of the Beck-Fiala bound for small $t$.

literature.title: B. Bukh, An improvement of the Beck-Fiala theorem, Combinatorics, Probability and Computing 25(3):380-398, 2016
literature.description: Proves $\mathrm{disc} \leq 2t - \log^{*} t$, the best known bound depending only on $t$.

literature.title: W. Banaszczyk, Balancing vectors and Gaussian measures of n-dimensional convex bodies, Random Structures & Algorithms 12(4):351-360, 1998
literature.description: Proves the vector-balancing theorem for convex bodies of Gaussian measure at least $1/2$; applied to a scaled $\ell_\infty$ ball it gives $O(\sqrt{\log n})$ for the Komlós problem and $O(\sqrt{k \log n})$ for degree-$k$ set systems.

literature.title: A. Newman, O. Neiman, A. Nikolov, Beck's three permutations conjecture: a counterexample and some consequences, FOCS 2012 (arXiv:1104.2922, Newman and Nikolov, 2011)
literature.description: Constructs three permutations of $[n]$ whose intervals have discrepancy $\Omega(\log n)$, disproving Beck's conjecture that $D(3, n) = O(1)$; derives lower bounds for rounding the Gilmore-Gomory LP for bin packing.

literature.title: N. Bansal, D. Dadush, S. Garg, An algorithm for Komlós conjecture matching Banaszczyk's bound, FOCS 2016; SIAM Journal on Computing 48(2):534-553, 2019
literature.description: First polynomial-time algorithm achieving Banaszczyk's $O(\sqrt{\log \min\{d, n\}})$ bound for the Komlós problem (and $O(\sqrt{t \log n})$ for Beck-Fiala).

literature.title: N. Bansal, S. Garg, Algorithmic discrepancy beyond partial coloring, STOC 2017; arXiv:1611.01805
literature.description: General algorithmic framework that overcomes the iterated-partial-coloring loss. For Tusnády's problem it improves the planar bound from $O(\log^{2.5} n)$ to $O(\log^2 n)$ and gives $O_d(\log^d n)$ for boxes in $\mathbb{R}^d$ (since improved to $O(\log^{d-1/2} n)$ by Nikolov). For the Steinitz problem it gives the first algorithm matching Banaszczyk's non-constructive $\ell_\infty$ bound and an algorithmic $O(\sqrt{d \log n})$ bound in the $\ell_2$ case.

literature.title: N. Bansal, H. Jiang, An improved bound for the Beck-Fiala conjecture, FOCS 2025; arXiv:2508.01937
literature.description: Proves discrepancy $O(\sqrt{k \log\log n})$ for $k$-sparse set systems with $k \geq \log^5 n$; superseded by the authors' follow-up arXiv:2508.03961 (which proves $O(\sqrt{k})$ for $k \geq \log^2 n$). Kept for chronology.

literature.title: N. Bansal, H. Jiang, Decoupling via affine spectral-independence: Beck-Fiala and Komlós bounds beyond Banaszczyk, arXiv:2508.03961, 2025
literature.description: Gives an algorithmic $\widetilde{O}(\log^{1/4} n)$ bound for the Komlós problem, the first improvement over Banaszczyk's $O(\sqrt{\log n})$, and proves the Beck-Fiala conjecture (discrepancy $O(\sqrt{k})$) for all degrees $k \geq \log^2 n$, together with an $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{k} + \sqrt{\log n})$ bound for every $k$.

literature.title: D. J. Altschuler, K. Tikhomirov, Online Beck-Fiala down to logarithmic sparsity, arXiv:2607.14238, 2026
literature.description: Extends the validity of the (offline) Beck-Fiala conjecture to column sparsity $t \geq (\log n)^{1+o(1)}$, i.e. $O(\sqrt{t})$ discrepancy, obtained by an efficient online algorithm minimizing prefix discrepancy (a Metropolis fixed-point walk). Essentially optimal for online methods since online prefix discrepancy is $\omega(\sqrt{t})$ for $t = o(\log n)$; also resolves online vector balancing in the Spencer setting.

literature.title: N. Bansal, A. Nikolov, Discrepancy theory: an algorithmic and geometric perspective, arXiv:2608.00140, 2026
literature.description: 2026 survey of combinatorial discrepancy (Komlós, Beck-Fiala, Tusnády, vector balancing and the algorithmic theory); cited here as the reference for the current state of these problems, in particular for Tusnády's problem ($\Omega(\log n) \leq d_2(n) \leq O(\log^2 n)$ in the plane, $\Omega(\log^{d-1} n) \leq d_d(n) \leq O(\log^{d-1/2} n)$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$) and for the state of the Komlós and Beck-Fiala conjectures before their resolution in arXiv:2609.11189 (September 2026).

literature.title: S. Guo, E. X. Fang, J. Lu, Vector balancing via directional total variation, arXiv:2609.11189, 2026
literature.description: Corollary 1.2: if $A \in \{0,1\}^{m \times n}$ has at most $t$ ones per column then $\mathrm{disc}(A) < 3\sqrt{2\pi t}$, for every positive integer $t$ and all $m, n$; this is the Beck-Fiala conjecture, derived from the Komlós bound $3\sqrt{2\pi}$ (Theorem 1.1) by scaling. Existential; no polynomial-time algorithm.

problems.verificationNotes: Re-verified on 2026-09-20 against http://aimpl.org/hereddiscrep/1/, the arXiv listings of the cited papers and the survey arXiv:2608.00140. Corrections made on 2026-09-20 following the comment by Richard Peng: the Bansal-Jiang identifier is arXiv:2508.03961 (not 2508.3961); the 2026 result of Altschuler-Tikhomirov (arXiv:2607.14238, $t \geq (\log n)^{1+o(1)}$) was added; a literature entry whose title carried an unrelated arXiv identifier (a quantum-information paper) was replaced by the correct Bansal-Garg reference arXiv:1611.01805; Google Scholar search links were replaced by DOI/arXiv links. In Altschuler-Tikhomirov's notation $A \in \{0,1\}^{n \times T}$ has column sparsity $d$; this record uses $t$ for the sparsity and $n$ for the number of elements. Status set to solved on 2026-09-20 on the basis of arXiv:2609.11189 (Guo-Fang-Lu, Corollary 1.2, checked against the full text: $\mathrm{disc}(A) = \sqrt{t}\,\mathrm{disc}(A/\sqrt{t}) < 3\sqrt{2\pi t}$ since the columns of $A/\sqrt{t}$ have Euclidean norm at most one); the paper is a preprint and its argument is existential.
problems.statusDetails: Solved (existentially) in September 2026: Guo, Fang and Lu (arXiv:2609.11189, Corollary 1.2) prove $\mathrm{disc} < 3\sqrt{2\pi t}$ for every set system of column sparsity $t$, for all $t, n, m$, as a consequence of their Komlós bound $3\sqrt{2\pi}$. History: Beck and Fiala (1981) proved $\mathrm{disc} \leq 2t - 1$; the best $n$-independent bounds before 2026 were $2t - 3$ (Bednarchak-Helm 1997), Helm (1999) and $2t - \log^{*} t$ (Bukh 2016). Banaszczyk (1998) gave $O(\sqrt{t \log n})$, made algorithmic by Bansal-Dadush-Garg (2016). Bansal and Jiang (arXiv:2508.03961, 2025) proved the conjecture algorithmically for $t \geq \log^2 n$ and $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{t} + \sqrt{\log n})$ for all $t$; Altschuler and Tikhomirov (arXiv:2607.14238, 2026) extended the algorithmic range to $t \geq (\log n)^{1+o(1)}$ with an online prefix-discrepancy algorithm. Open: a polynomial-time algorithm achieving $O(\sqrt{t})$ for $t \leq \log n$, and the optimal constant. The random-system version is Problem 1.2.

problems.sourceStatement: Each element $i\in [n]$ lies in $t$ randomly selected sets from $\mathcal{S}$. They show that when $m\ge n$, hereditary discrepancy of the set system is $O(\sqrt{t\log t})$ whp. When $n\ge m^t$, hereditary discrepancy is $O(1)$. An open question is to explore this setting for the remaining range of parameters i.e. when $n^{1/t} < m < n$.
problems.problem: Determine the (hereditary) discrepancy of a random $t$-sparse set system: $n$ elements, $m$ sets, each element placed in $t$ sets chosen uniformly at random. Is it $O(\sqrt{t})$ with high probability for all $n, m$ and all $t$, and in particular in the intermediate regime $n^{1/t} \ll m \ll n$ for small $t$?
problems.wordDescription: A natural test case for the Beck-Fiala conjecture is the random $t$-sparse model in which every element is put into $t$ uniformly random sets. Ezra and Lovett (2015) showed that the hereditary discrepancy is $O(\sqrt{t \log t})$ when $m \geq n$ and $O(1)$ when $n \gg m^t$, leaving open the intermediate regime. Subsequent work essentially settled the discrepancy of the whole system for moderately large $t$: Potukuchi (2018) proved $O(\sqrt{t})$ almost surely for $m = n$ and $\log^{10} n \ll t \ll \sqrt{n}$, and Bansal and Meka (2019) proved a tight $O(\sqrt{t})$ bound for the entire range of $n$ and $m$ provided $t = \Omega((\log\log m)^2)$. In the related regime of many columns, Franks and Saks showed discrepancy at most $2$ for random $t$-sparse matrices once $n = \Omega(m^3 \log^2 m)$, Hoberg and Rothvoss showed discrepancy at most $1$ for the i.i.d. Bernoulli$(p)$ model when $n \geq \Theta(m^2 \log m)$, and Potukuchi lowered this threshold to $n = \Omega(m \log m)$ for $p = 1/2$. The remaining gaps (very small $t$ in the intermediate range $n^{1/t} \ll m \ll n$, and the hereditary version of the newer bounds) were closed from the worst-case side in September 2026: Guo, Fang and Lu (arXiv:2609.11189, Corollary 1.2) prove $\mathrm{disc}(A) < 3\sqrt{2\pi t}$ for every $0/1$ matrix of column sparsity $t$, deterministically and for all $n, m$; since column-restrictions remain $t$-sparse, $\mathrm{herdisc}(A) < 3\sqrt{2\pi t}$ as well. The random model therefore has (hereditary) discrepancy $O(\sqrt{t})$ in every regime. What remains is the exact order in regimes where the truth is $o(\sqrt{t})$ (e.g. $O(1)$ for $n \gg m^t$), and efficient algorithms, since the Guo-Fang-Lu argument is non-constructive.
problems.mathematicalConditions: Model $\mathcal{H}_1(n, m, t)$. Elements $X = [n]$, sets $S_1, \dots, S_m$; independently for each $x \in X$, a uniformly random $t$-subset $T_x \subseteq [m]$ is chosen and $x$ is placed in exactly the sets $S_j$, $j \in T_x$. Let $A \in \{0,1\}^{m \times n}$ be the incidence matrix. $\mathrm{disc}(A) = \min_{x \in \{-1,1\}^n} \|Ax\|_\infty$; $\mathrm{herdisc}(A) = \max_{J \subseteq [n]} \mathrm{disc}(A_J)$ where $A_J$ is the column-restriction to $J$. All statements are 'with high probability' (w.h.p.), i.e. with probability $1 - o(1)$ as $n \to \infty$, with $m = m(n)$ and $t = t(n)$. Question. Is $\mathrm{disc}(A) = O(\sqrt{t})$ w.h.p. for all $m, t$; and is the same true for $\mathrm{herdisc}(A)$? Benchmarks. $\mathrm{herdisc}(A) = O(\sqrt{t \log t})$ w.h.p. if $m \geq n$, and $\mathrm{herdisc}(A) = O(1)$ w.h.p. if $n \gg m^t$ (Ezra-Lovett 2015). $\mathrm{disc}(A) = O(\sqrt{t})$ almost surely when $m = n$ and $\log^{10} n \ll t \ll \sqrt{n}$ (Potukuchi 2018). $\mathrm{disc}(A) = O(\sqrt{t})$ for all $n, m$ whenever $t = \Omega((\log\log m)^2)$ (Bansal-Meka 2019, stated as tight: the discrepancy is also $\Omega(\sqrt{t})$ w.h.p. in the regimes where the sets have size $\gg t$). Many-columns regime of $\mathcal{H}_1$: $\mathrm{disc}(A) \leq 2$ w.h.p. once $n = \Omega(m^3 \log^2 m)$ (Franks-Saks 2020, improving Ezra-Lovett's $n \geq m^t$). Related model $\mathcal{H}_2(n, m, p)$: the entries of $A \in \{0,1\}^{m \times n}$ are i.i.d. Bernoulli$(p)$; $\mathrm{disc}(A) \leq 1$ w.h.p. when $n \geq \Theta(m^2 \log m)$ (Hoberg-Rothvoss 2019), and $\mathrm{disc}(A) \leq 1$ a.s. when $p = 1/2$ and $n = \Omega(m \log m)$ (Potukuchi 2018, answering a question of Hoberg-Rothvoss). Complete resolution. A proof that, in $\mathcal{H}_1(n,m,t)$, $\mathrm{disc}(A) = O(\sqrt{t})$ w.h.p. for all $m = m(n)$ and all $1 \leq t \leq m$ (any growth of $t$), together with either the same for $\mathrm{herdisc}(A)$ or a proof that $\mathrm{herdisc}(A) = \omega(\sqrt{t})$ w.h.p. in some regime; or a disproof exhibiting a regime with $\mathrm{disc}(A) = \omega(\sqrt{t})$ w.h.p. Minimal progress that counts as a solution of this record. Any of: (i) $\mathrm{disc}(A) = O(\sqrt{t})$ w.h.p. for all $m$ and all $t \geq t_0$ with $t_0 = o((\log\log m)^2)$ (e.g. $t_0 = O(1)$ or $t_0 = O(\log\log m)$); (ii) for fixed $t \geq 3$, determining whether $\mathrm{disc}(A) = O(1)$ w.h.p. throughout $n^{1/t} \ll m \ll n$ (or finding a sub-regime where it is not); (iii) $\mathrm{herdisc}(A) = O(\sqrt{t})$ w.h.p. for $m \geq n$ (removing the $\sqrt{\log t}$ of Ezra-Lovett) or in any intermediate regime not covered by Ezra-Lovett; (iv) a polynomial-time algorithm finding a coloring of discrepancy $O(\sqrt{t})$ w.h.p. in a regime where only an existential bound is known. Improvements of constants or of the exponent $10$ in $\log^{10} n$ do not count. Resolution (September 2026). Guo-Fang-Lu (arXiv:2609.11189, Corollary 1.2) give $\mathrm{disc}(A) < 3\sqrt{2\pi t}$ for every $0/1$ matrix with at most $t$ ones per column, hence for every realization of $\mathcal{H}_1(n, m, t)$ and every column-restriction $A_J$: $\mathrm{herdisc}(A) < 3\sqrt{2\pi t}$ surely, for all $m$ and all $t$. This meets the complete-resolution criterion (both $\mathrm{disc}$ and $\mathrm{herdisc}$ are $O(\sqrt{t})$ for all $m, t$) and items (i) and (iii); the record is solved. Still open: item (iv) (a polynomial-time algorithm), and the exact order of $\mathrm{disc}(A)$ in regimes where it is $o(\sqrt{t})$.

literature.title: E. Ezra, S. Lovett, On the Beck-Fiala conjecture for random set systems, APPROX/RANDOM 2015; Random Structures & Algorithms 54(4):665-675, 2019
literature.description: Introduces the random $t$-sparse model and proves $\mathrm{herdisc} = O(\sqrt{t \log t})$ w.h.p. for $m \geq n$ and $O(1)$ for $n \gg m^t$.

literature.title: A. Potukuchi, Discrepancy in random hypergraph models, arXiv:1811.01491, 2018
literature.description: In the model where every element lies in exactly $t$ random sets, proves discrepancy $O(\sqrt{t})$ almost surely when $m = n$ and $\log^{10} n \ll t \ll \sqrt{n}$ (improving Ezra-Lovett in this range); in the i.i.d. model with $p = 1/2$ and $n = \Omega(m \log m)$ proves discrepancy at most $1$, answering a question of Hoberg-Rothvoss.

literature.title: N. Bansal, R. Meka, On the discrepancy of random low degree set systems, SODA 2019; Random Structures & Algorithms 57(3):695-705, 2020
literature.description: Proves a tight $O(\sqrt{t})$ discrepancy bound for the random $t$-sparse model for the entire range of $n$ and $m$ under $t = \Omega((\log\log m)^2)$.

literature.title: R. Hoberg, T. Rothvoss, A Fourier-analytic approach for the discrepancy of random set systems, SODA 2019; arXiv:1806.04484
literature.description: Introduces Fourier-analytic discrepancy bounds and applies them to the i.i.d. Bernoulli$(p)$ model: for $n \geq \Theta(m^2 \log m)$ the discrepancy is at most $1$ w.h.p. (previously $O(1)$ only for $n \gg m^t$ by Ezra-Lovett); the threshold was lowered to $n = \Omega(m \log m)$ for $p = 1/2$ by Potukuchi.

literature.title: C. Franks, M. Saks, On the discrepancy of random matrices with many columns, Random Structures & Algorithms 57(1):64-96, 2020
literature.description: Local-limit-theorem approach (via Fourier analysis) to the discrepancy of random $m \times n$ matrices with i.i.d. columns. For random $t$-sparse matrices ($t$ ones per column) shows $\ell_\infty$-discrepancy at most $2$ w.h.p. once $n = \Omega(m^3 \log^2 m)$, improving the $n \geq m^t$ requirement of Ezra-Lovett.

literature.title: S. Guo, E. X. Fang, J. Lu, Vector balancing via directional total variation, arXiv:2609.11189, 2026
literature.description: Corollary 1.2: $\mathrm{disc}(A) < 3\sqrt{2\pi t}$ for every $0/1$ matrix with at most $t$ ones per column (the Beck-Fiala conjecture), derived from the Komlós bound $3\sqrt{2\pi}$. Applied to every realization of $\mathcal{H}_1(n,m,t)$ and every column-restriction, it gives $\mathrm{herdisc}(A) = O(\sqrt{t})$ for all $n, m, t$. Existential.

problems.statusDetails: Solved in September 2026 by the worst-case Beck-Fiala theorem of Guo, Fang and Lu (arXiv:2609.11189, Corollary 1.2): every $t$-column-sparse $0/1$ matrix has $\mathrm{disc} < 3\sqrt{2\pi t}$, hence $\mathrm{herdisc} = O(\sqrt{t})$ for the random system in every regime of $n, m, t$ (existentially). problems.sourceStatement: Given a set system where the elements are the vertices of the hypercube $\{0,1\}^n$. Corresponding to each vertex $v$, there is a set $S_v$ which is generated by picking a random subset of the neighbours of $v$ in the hypercube. What is the discrepancy of this set system?
problems.problem: Determine the discrepancy (in expectation / with high probability) of the set system on the vertices of the hypercube $\{0,1\}^n$ in which each vertex $v$ is assigned a set $S_v$ consisting of a random subset of its neighbours in the hypercube.
problems.wordDescription: This problem, posed by Shachar Lovett at the workshop, concerns the discrepancy of a natural random set system supported on the $n$-dimensional hypercube. The elements are the $2^n$ vertices, and each set $S_v$ is formed by independently picking a random subset of the neighbours of $v$. The status note on the AimPL page points out that in the deterministic variant where $S_v$ is the full set of neighbours of $v$, there is an easy coloring with discrepancy 1: color each vertex by the parity of its first $n/2$ bits. The question is what happens when each $S_v$ is a random (and therefore typically about half-size, roughly $n/2$ of the $n$ neighbours) subset of the neighbourhood: the resulting system is $\Theta(n)$-sparse on $2^n$ elements, so generic sparse-system bounds give only $\sqrt{n}\,\mathrm{poly}(\log n)$, while the deterministic system has discrepancy $1$. No published treatment of this specific model was located during verification. However, every vertex $u$ lies in at most $n$ of the sets (one for each neighbour $v$ of $u$), so the Beck-Fiala theorem of Guo, Fang and Lu (arXiv:2609.11189, September 2026) gives discrepancy less than $3\sqrt{2\pi n} = O(\sqrt{n})$ for every realization; this is the $O(\sqrt{\text{sparsity}})$ upper bound that this record set as its minimal-progress criterion. Whether the truth is $O(1)$, as in the full-neighbourhood case, or $\Theta(\sqrt{n})$, remains open, as does an efficient algorithm.
problems.mathematicalConditions: Setting. Let $Q_d = \{0,1\}^d$ be the vertex set of the $d$-dimensional hypercube (the AimPL statement writes $n$ for the dimension; we write $d$ and set $N = 2^d = |Q_d|$), and for $v \in Q_d$ let $N(v) = \{u \in Q_d : \mathrm{dist}_H(u, v) = 1\}$ be its Hamming neighbourhood, $|N(v)| = d$. Random model. Independently for every $v \in Q_d$, let $S_v \subseteq N(v)$ be a uniformly random subset (equivalently, each neighbour of $v$ is included in $S_v$ independently with probability $1/2$; the model with inclusion probability $p \in (0,1)$ is the natural generalization). This defines the random set system $\mathcal{S} = \{S_v : v \in Q_d\}$ on ground set $Q_d$, with $N$ elements and $N$ sets, each element in $\mathrm{Bin}(d, 1/2)$ sets and each set of size $\mathrm{Bin}(d, 1/2)$; its incidence matrix $A \in \{0,1\}^{N \times N}$ is a random sub-matrix of the adjacency matrix of $Q_d$. Quantities. $\mathrm{disc}(\mathcal{S}) = \min_{\chi : Q_d \to \{-1,1\}} \max_{v \in Q_d} \left|\sum_{u \in S_v} \chi(u)\right|$ and $\mathrm{herdisc}(\mathcal{S}) = \max_{J \subseteq Q_d} \mathrm{disc}(\mathcal{S}|_J)$. All statements about $\mathcal{S}$ are 'with high probability' (w.h.p.), i.e. with probability $1 - o(1)$ as $d \to \infty$. Question (as posed). Determine the order of growth of $\mathrm{disc}(\mathcal{S})$ w.h.p. as a function of $d$. Benchmarks. Deterministic full-neighbourhood case $S_v = N(v)$: $\mathrm{disc} \leq 1$ via $\chi(v) = (-1)^{v_1 + \dots + v_{\lfloor d/2 \rfloor}}$ (the parity of the first $\lfloor d/2 \rfloor$ bits; recorded on the AimPL page). Generic bounds for the random system: a uniformly random $\chi$ gives $O(\sqrt{d \log N}) = O(d)$, the trivial bound; the system is $d$-sparse in both rows and columns, so the Beck-Fiala theorem gives $\mathrm{disc} \leq 2d - 1$, Banaszczyk's theorem gives $O(\sqrt{d \log N}) = O(d)$, the Lovász Local Lemma for $d$-sparse, $O(d)$-uniform systems gives $O(\sqrt{d \log d})$ (Problem 1.7), and the Bansal-Jiang bound $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{t} + \sqrt{\log N})$ for column sparsity $t$ gives $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{d})$ (here $t \leq d = \log_2 N$), where $\widetilde{O}$ hides $\mathrm{poly}(\log\log N) = \mathrm{poly}(\log d)$ factors; the $O(\sqrt{t})$ results for $t \geq (\log N)^{1+o(1)}$ do not apply, since $t \approx d/2 = \Theta(\log N)$ sits exactly at the logarithmic threshold. Since every $u \in Q_d$ lies in at most $d$ sets (column sparsity $\leq d$ for every realization), the Beck-Fiala theorem of Guo-Fang-Lu (2026) gives $\mathrm{disc}(\mathcal{S}) \leq \mathrm{herdisc}(\mathcal{S}) < 3\sqrt{2\pi d}$ surely. No super-constant lower bound is recorded for this model. Thus the known range is $1 \leq \mathrm{disc}(\mathcal{S}) < 3\sqrt{2\pi d}$, and the problem is whether the answer is $O(1)$, $\Theta(\sqrt{d})$ (as for random $\Theta(d)$-sparse systems, cf. Problem 1.2), or in between. Complete resolution. Determining $\mathrm{disc}(\mathcal{S})$ up to constant factors w.h.p. (for $p = 1/2$), e.g. proving $\mathrm{disc}(\mathcal{S}) = O(1)$ w.h.p., or $\mathrm{disc}(\mathcal{S}) = \Theta(\sqrt{d})$ w.h.p. Minimal progress that counts as a solution of this record. Any of: (i) an upper bound $\mathrm{disc}(\mathcal{S}) = O(\sqrt{d})$ w.h.p. (removing the $\mathrm{poly}(\log d)$ factors, i.e. the Beck-Fiala conjecture for this model), or any bound $o(\sqrt{d})$; (ii) a lower bound $\mathrm{disc}(\mathcal{S}) = \omega(1)$ w.h.p., or a lower bound $\Omega(\sqrt{d})$ w.h.p. (showing the random system is genuinely harder than the full-neighbourhood system); (iii) the same statements for $\mathrm{herdisc}(\mathcal{S})$, or for the model with a general inclusion probability $p = p(d)$ in a range of $p$ including $p = 1/2$; (iv) a polynomial-in-$N$-time algorithm that w.h.p. produces a coloring of discrepancy $O(\sqrt{d})$. Improving only constants in the trivial bounds does not count. Resolution status (September 2026). Item (i), the upper bound $\mathrm{disc}(\mathcal{S}) = O(\sqrt{d})$ (indeed $\mathrm{herdisc}(\mathcal{S}) < 3\sqrt{2\pi d}$ for every realization), is met by Guo-Fang-Lu (arXiv:2609.11189, Corollary 1.2), so the record counts as solved. The complete-resolution question ($O(1)$ versus $\Theta(\sqrt{d})$ w.h.p.), the lower-bound item (ii) and the algorithmic item (iv) remain open.

problems.sourceStatement: a) discrepancy of k-permutations: For $k=3$, $[NNN'12]$ showed a lower bound of $\Omega(\log n)$ where $n$ is the number of elements in the ground set. For general $k$, we know that the answer lies in $[\sqrt{k}+\log n,\sqrt{k}\log n]$. An open question is to clsoe this gap. b) discrepancy of k-random permutations: A lower bound of $\Omega(\sqrt{k})$ is known.
problems.problem: Determine the maximum discrepancy of a $k$-permutation family on $n$ elements (the set system of all intervals of $k$ given permutations of $[n]$), and determine the discrepancy of $k$ uniformly random permutations.
problems.wordDescription: A $k$-permutation family is the set system whose sets are all intervals of $k$ permutations of the integers $1, \dots, n$. Beck conjectured (c. 1987) that three permutations always admit a constant-discrepancy coloring; Newman and Nikolov refuted this with a recursive construction of three permutations with discrepancy $\Omega(\log n)$ (with Neiman, they also showed consequences for rounding the Gilmore-Gomory bin-packing LP). Spencer, Srinivasan and Tetali proved the upper bound $O(\sqrt{k}\log n)$ for $k$ permutations. For fixed $k \geq 3$ the lower bound $\Omega(\log n)$ transfers from the $k = 3$ construction, so the maximal discrepancy of a $k$-permutation family is known to lie between $\sqrt{k} + \log n$ (up to constants) and $\sqrt{k}\log n$; closing this gap is the open question. For $k$ random permutations, a lower bound of $\Omega(\sqrt{k})$ is reported on the AimPL page.
problems.mathematicalConditions: Setting. For permutations $\pi_1, \dots, \pi_k$ of $[n]$ let $\mathcal{P}(\pi_1, \dots, \pi_k)$ be the set system consisting of all intervals $\{\pi_j(a), \pi_j(a+1), \dots, \pi_j(b)\}$, $1 \leq j \leq k$, $1 \leq a \leq b \leq n$ (equivalently all prefixes, since discrepancy of prefixes and of intervals differ by a factor at most $2$). Let $D(k, n) = \max_{\pi_1, \dots, \pi_k} \mathrm{disc}(\mathcal{P}(\pi_1, \dots, \pi_k))$ and let $D_{\mathrm{rand}}(k, n)$ be the discrepancy when $\pi_1, \dots, \pi_k$ are independent uniformly random permutations (statements w.h.p. as $n \to \infty$). Problem. Determine $D(k, n)$ up to constant factors for all $k = k(n)$, and $D_{\mathrm{rand}}(k, n)$ for the random model. Benchmarks (worst case). $D(1, n) = 1$, $D(2, n) \leq 2$ (Spencer). $D(3, n) = \Omega(\log n)$ (Newman-Nikolov 2011, disproving Beck's conjecture; simplified by Franks 2018). Upper bound: $D(k, n) = O(\sqrt{k} \log n)$ (Spencer-Srinivasan-Tetali, unpublished, via partial coloring; algorithmic by Bansal 2010). Lower bound: $D(k, n) = \Omega(\sqrt{k})$ for $k \leq n$ (from $k$ random permutations, see below), and $D(k, n) \geq D(3, n) = \Omega(\log n)$ for $k \geq 3$. Note that in the prefix formulation every element lies in $\Theta(kn)$ sets, so Beck-Fiala/Banaszczyk-type sparse bounds do not apply directly. Benchmarks (random). For $k$ independent uniformly random permutations the discrepancy is $\Omega(\sqrt{k})$ w.h.p. (recorded on the AimPL page for $k \leq n$) and $O(\sqrt{k}\log n)$ by the worst-case bound; whether $D_{\mathrm{rand}}(k, n) = O(\sqrt{k})$ is open. Complete resolution. Determining $D(k, n)$ up to constant factors for all $3 \leq k \leq n$ (in particular deciding whether $D(k, n) = \Theta(\sqrt{k} \log n)$, $\Theta(\sqrt{k \log n})$, or something in between), and determining $D_{\mathrm{rand}}(k, n)$ up to constants. Minimal progress that counts as a solution of this record. Any of: (i) an upper bound $D(k, n) = O(\sqrt{k}\, (\log n)^{\gamma})$ with $\gamma < 1$ for all $k$, or a lower bound $D(k, n) = \Omega(\sqrt{k}\,(\log n)^{\gamma})$ with $\gamma > 0$ for all $k$ in an infinite range; (ii) for fixed $k \geq 3$, determining $D(k, n)$ up to constants (for $k = 3$ the bounds $\Omega(\log n) \leq D(3, n) \leq O(\log n)$ already match, so this item concerns $k \geq 4$); (iii) $D_{\mathrm{rand}}(k, n) = O(\sqrt{k}\,(\log n)^{\gamma})$ with $\gamma < 1$ w.h.p., or a lower bound $\omega(\sqrt{k})$ w.h.p. in the random model; (iv) a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm matching the best known bound where only randomized or existential arguments are known.

literature.title: J. Spencer, A. Srinivasan, P. Tetali, The discrepancy of permutation families, unpublished manuscript (c. 2001)
literature.description: Proves $\mathrm{disc} = O(\sqrt{k}\log n)$ for the intervals of $k$ permutations via partial coloring. No stable URL exists for this manuscript; it is cited in this form by Newman-Nikolov, Eisenbrand-Pálvölgyi-Rothvoß and the 2026 survey arXiv:2608.00140.

literature.title: A. Newman, O. Neiman, A. Nikolov, Beck's three permutations conjecture: a counterexample and some consequences, FOCS 2012 (arXiv:1104.2922, Newman and Nikolov, 2011)

problems.sourceStatement: Given matrices $A_1,...,A_n \in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ satisfying $||A_i||_{op} \le 1$ where $||.||_{op}$ is the operator norm of matrices. Do there exists signs $\epsilon_1,...,\epsilon_n\in\{-1,1\}$ s.t. $||\sum_{i=1}^n\epsilon_i A_i || =O(\sqrt{n})$.
problems.problem: Prove the Matrix Spencer conjecture: for any symmetric $n \times n$ matrices $A_1, \dots, A_n$ of operator norm at most $1$, there exist signs $\epsilon \in \{-1,1\}^n$ with $\left\|\sum_i \epsilon_i A_i\right\|_{\mathrm{op}} = O(\sqrt{n})$ (more generally, $O(\sqrt{n \max(1, \log(d/n))})$ for $d \times d$ matrices).
problems.wordDescription: The Matrix Spencer conjecture, posed by Zouzias (2012) and by Meka (2014), asks for a non-commutative analogue of Spencer's 'six standard deviations' theorem: the matrix Chernoff bound gives $O(\sqrt{n \log d})$ for random signs, and the conjecture asserts that the logarithmic factor can be removed, exactly as Spencer removed it in the scalar case. It contains Spencer's theorem (diagonal matrices). Progress has come in structured special cases: matrices of small Frobenius norm or low rank (Hopkins-Raghavendra-Shetty 2022, $\|A_i\|_F \leq n^{1/4}$; Dadush-Jiang-Reis 2022, rank $r$ with $r d \leq n$ for $d \times d$ matrices, plus block-diagonal and Schatten-norm variants), matrices of rank at most $n/\log^3 n$ via matrix concentration and partial coloring (Bansal-Jiang-Meka 2023), and, in 2026, two algebraic special cases: Bandeira and Bölcskei proved the 'Group Spencer' conjecture (the left regular representation of any finite group $G$ admits signs $\epsilon \in \{\pm1\}^G$ with $\|\sum_g \epsilon_g \rho(g)\| \leq C\sqrt{|G|}$), and Akbas and Sra proved the conjecture for any family of contractions inside a finite-dimensional $C^{*}$-algebra of complex dimension $O(n)$, which contains the group case and is stable under low-rank perturbations. The general conjecture remains open; for general families the best known bound remains $O(\sqrt{n \log d})$ from the non-commutative Khintchine/matrix Chernoff inequality (with the trivial $d = n$ case giving $O(\sqrt{n \log n})$).
problems.mathematicalConditions: Setting. Let $\mathcal{S}_d$ be the real symmetric (or complex Hermitian) $d \times d$ matrices with operator norm $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{op}} \leq 1$. For $A_1, \dots, A_n \in \mathcal{S}_d$ let $\mathrm{disc}(A_1, \dots, A_n) = \min_{\epsilon \in \{-1,1\}^n} \left\|\sum_{i=1}^n \epsilon_i A_i\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ and let $\mathrm{MS}(n, d)$ be its supremum over all such families. Conjecture (Matrix Spencer). $\mathrm{MS}(n, d) \leq C\sqrt{n \max(1, \log(d/n))}$ for an absolute constant $C$; in particular $\mathrm{MS}(n, n) = O(\sqrt{n})$ (the AimPL formulation, $d = n$). Benchmarks. Lower bound $\mathrm{MS}(n, d) = \Omega(\sqrt{n \max(1, \log(d/n))})$ from diagonal matrices (Spencer's theorem is tight). Upper bounds: $\mathrm{MS}(n, d) = O(\sqrt{n \log d})$ (matrix Chernoff / non-commutative Khintchine, random signs). Special cases proved: (a) Hopkins-Raghavendra-Shetty 2022: the conjecture whenever $\|A_i\|_F \leq n^{1/4}$ for all $i$ (in particular whenever $\mathrm{rank}(A_i) \leq \sqrt{n}$), via quantum communication complexity; Dadush-Jiang-Reis 2022: for $d \times d$ matrices of rank at most $r$ the algorithmic bound $O(\sqrt{n \log\min(rd/n, r)})$, hence the conjecture when $r d \leq n$; for block-diagonal families with block size $h$ the bound $O(\sqrt{n \log(hd/n)})$; and Schatten-norm variants, all via a partial-coloring (mirror-descent) framework; (b) Bansal-Jiang-Meka 2023: $O(\sqrt{n})$ whenever $\mathrm{rank}(A_i) \leq r$ for all $i$ with $r \leq n / \log^{3} n$; (c) Zouzias 2012: an algorithmic $O(\sqrt{n \log d})$ via a matrix hyperbolic-cosine potential; (d) Bandeira-Kunisky-Mixon-Zeng 2022/24: the group version for finite simple groups; (e) Bandeira-Bölcskei 2026: the group version for every finite group $G$ ($A_g = \rho(g)$, $\rho$ the left regular representation, $n = d = |G|$); (f) Akbas-Sra 2026: $O(\sqrt{n})$ whenever $A_1, \dots, A_n$ are contractions in a finite-dimensional $C^{*}$-algebra $\mathcal{A} \subseteq \mathbb{C}^{d \times d}$ with $\dim_{\mathbb{C}} \mathcal{A} \leq C n$ (including all matrices simultaneously block-diagonalizable with blocks of total squared size $O(n)$, and low-rank perturbations thereof). All of these are special cases; the general statement is open. Complete resolution. A proof of $\mathrm{MS}(n, d) = O(\sqrt{n \max(1, \log(d/n))})$ for all $n, d$ (or even just $\mathrm{MS}(n, n) = O(\sqrt{n})$), or a disproof: families with $\mathrm{disc} / \sqrt{n \max(1,\log(d/n))} \to \infty$. Minimal progress that counts as a solution of this record. Any of: (i) $\mathrm{MS}(n, n) = O(\sqrt{n}\,(\log n)^{\gamma})$ for some constant $\gamma < 1/2$, for arbitrary symmetric contractions; (ii) the conjecture for all families with $\mathrm{rank}(A_i) \leq r$ whenever $r \leq n/(\log n)^{\gamma}$ for some constant $\gamma < 3$ (improving the rank threshold of Bansal-Jiang-Meka by a polylogarithmic factor), or for $r \leq n/(\log\log n)^{O(1)}$; (iii) the conjecture for all families lying in a $C^{*}$-algebra of dimension $\leq n^{1+\delta}$ for some fixed $\delta > 0$, or for all families of commuting-up-to-low-rank type strictly extending Akbas-Sra; (iv) a super-$\sqrt{n}$ lower bound $\mathrm{MS}(n, n) = \omega(\sqrt{n})$; (v) a polynomial-time algorithm achieving $O(\sqrt{n})$ in a structured case where only an existential proof is known (e.g. the Bandeira-Bölcskei group case). Improving constants alone does not count.

literature.title: A. Zouzias, A matrix hyperbolic cosine algorithm and applications, ICALP 2012 (LNCS 7391), pp. 846-858; arXiv:1103.2793
literature.description: Derandomizes the matrix Chernoff bound via a matrix hyperbolic-cosine potential and explicitly poses the Matrix Spencer question ($O(\sqrt{n})$ for $n$ symmetric $n \times n$ contractions).

literature.title: R. Meka, Discrepancy and beating the union bound, Windows on Theory blog, 7 Feb 2014
literature.description: Blog post formulating the Matrix Spencer conjecture as 'beating the union bound' in the matrix Chernoff inequality, in analogy with Spencer's theorem.

literature.title: S. B. Hopkins, P. Raghavendra, A. Shetty, Matrix discrepancy from quantum communication, STOC 2022; arXiv:2110.10099
literature.description: Uses quantum communication complexity to prove the Matrix Spencer conjecture whenever $\|A_i\|_F \leq n^{1/4}$ for all $i$ (in particular for matrices of rank at most $\sqrt{n}$), with a polynomial-time algorithm based on partial coloring and semidefinite programming; also shows the full conjecture is implied by a conjecture in quantum communication complexity.

literature.title: D. Dadush, H. Jiang, V. Reis, A new framework for matrix discrepancy: partial coloring bounds via mirror descent, STOC 2022; arXiv:2111.03171
literature.description: Partial-coloring framework for matrix discrepancy via mirror descent; for $m \times m$ matrices of rank at most $r$ efficiently finds signs with $\|\sum x_i A_i\| = O(\sqrt{n \log\min(rm/n, r)})$, proving the Matrix Spencer conjecture when $rm \leq n$; gives $O(\sqrt{n \log(hm/n)})$ for block-diagonal matrices with block size $h$, extensions to Schatten norms, and a reduction of the full conjecture to the existence of a quantum relative entropy net on the spectraplex.

literature.title: N. Bansal, H. Jiang, R. Meka, Resolving Matrix Spencer conjecture up to poly-logarithmic rank, STOC 2023; SIAM Journal on Computing (STOC 2023 special section), 2024; arXiv:2208.11286
literature.description: Proves the Matrix Spencer conjecture ($O(\sqrt{n})$ for $n$ symmetric $n \times n$ contractions) whenever all matrices have rank at most $n / \log^3 n$, via the matrix concentration inequalities of Bandeira-Boedihardjo-van Handel and partial coloring.

literature.title: A. S. Bandeira, D. Kunisky, D. G. Mixon, X. Zeng, On the concentration of Gaussian Cayley matrices, arXiv:2212.00066, 2022 (published 2024)
literature.description: Introduces the 'Group Spencer' conjecture for the left regular representation of a finite group and proves it for finite simple groups.

literature.title: A. S. Bandeira, H. Bölcskei, Matrix discrepancy for representations of finite groups, arXiv:2606.12181, 2026
literature.description: Proves the group version of the Matrix Spencer conjecture for every finite group $G$: there are signs $\epsilon \in \{\pm1\}^G$ with $\|\sum_{g \in G} \epsilon_g \rho(g)\| \leq C\sqrt{|G|}$, $\rho$ the left regular representation, via Peter-Weyl decomposition, intrinsic-freeness inequalities and iterated partial coloring. A structured special case; the general conjecture remains open.

literature.title: E. Akbas, S. Sra, An algebraic Matrix Spencer theorem, arXiv:2606.16005, 2026
literature.description: Representation-theoretic approach to matrix discrepancy: for contractions $A_1, \dots, A_n$ in a finite-dimensional $C^{*}$-algebra $\mathcal{A}$ with $\dim_{\mathbb{C}} \mathcal{A} \lesssim n$ there are signs with $\|\sum_i x_i A_i\| = O(\sqrt{n})$; this contains the Group Spencer conjecture and extends to low-rank perturbations. A structured special case; the general conjecture remains open.

problems.sourceStatement: Given vectors $v_1,...,v_n\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and a norm $X$ satisfying $\sum_{i=1}^n v_i=0$ and $||v_i||_X\le 1$ for all $i$. Define $S_n(X,d)=min_{\pi\in S^n}max_{k=1,...,n}|| \sum_{i=1}^k v_{\pi(i)}||_X$ where $S^n$ is the set of all permutations of $[n]$. Let $S(X,d)=sup_n S_n(X,d)$. Then, $S(X,d) =O(\sqrt{d})$.
problems.problem: Steinitz problem: for a norm $\|\cdot\|$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, determine the Steinitz constant $S(\|\cdot\|, d)$, the least $C$ such that every finite family of vectors of norm at most $1$ summing to zero can be ordered so that all partial sums have norm at most $C$. Steinitz's lemma gives $S \leq d$ for every norm (and this is tight up to constants for some norms, e.g. $S(\ell_1^d) \geq (d+1)/2$); the conjectured $O(\sqrt{d})$ is specific to the Euclidean norm (and is also asked for $\ell_\infty$), where the current record is Banaszczyk's $O(\sqrt{d} + \sqrt{\log n})$. Also sought: efficient algorithms achieving these bounds.
problems.wordDescription: Steinitz's lemma (1913) states that any zero-sum sequence of vectors in the unit ball of a $d$-dimensional normed space can be reordered so that every partial sum has norm at most $d$ (Grinberg-Sevastyanov 1980, sharpening earlier constants; for symmetric norms Sevastyanov obtained $d - 1 + 1/d$). This is tight up to constants for general norms: e.g. for $\ell_1$ the Steinitz constant is at least $(d+1)/2$. The open question is about specific norms. For the Euclidean norm it is conjectured that the Steinitz constant is $O(\sqrt{d})$; Banaszczyk (2012) proved $O(\sqrt{d} + \sqrt{\log n})$ non-constructively, matching the conjecture when $d \geq \log n$, and the lower bound is $\Omega(\sqrt{d})$. For $\ell_\infty$ the analogous $O(\sqrt{d})$ question is open as well. The algorithmic side has advanced recently: Bansal-Garg (2017) gave an efficient $O(\sqrt{d \log n})$ algorithm for $\ell_2$ (and an algorithm matching Banaszczyk's non-constructive bound for $\ell_\infty$), and Dutta, Jha and Jiang (2026) gave an efficient algorithm achieving the conjectured $O(\sqrt{d})$ for the $\ell_2$ Steinitz (and prefix-discrepancy) problem whenever $d \geq \Omega(\log^7 n)$. Ambrus and Heck (2025) relate the zero-sum Steinitz problem to its variant for nearly-unit, not necessarily zero-sum families, and give a detailed account of the known bounds ($d$ for general norms, $d - 1 + 1/d$ for symmetric norms, $(d+1)/2$ for $\ell_1$, $\sqrt{d+3}/2$ for $\ell_2$). The workshop comment refers to the then-current algorithmic guarantee $\sqrt{d}\log n$.
problems.mathematicalConditions: Setting. For a norm $\|\cdot\|_X$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with unit ball $B_X$, and vectors $v_1, \dots, v_n \in B_X$ with $\sum_i v_i = 0$, define $S(v_1, \dots, v_n; X) = \min_{\pi \in \mathfrak{S}_n} \max_{1 \leq k \leq n} \left\|\sum_{i=1}^k v_{\pi(i)}\right\|_X$; let $S_n(X, d) = \sup S(v_1, \dots, v_n; X)$ over all such families of $n$ vectors and $S(X, d) = \sup_n S_n(X, d)$ (the Steinitz constant of $X$). Known for general norms. $S(X, d) \leq d$ for every norm (Steinitz 1913 with constant $2d$; Sevastyanov 1978 and Grinberg-Sevastyanov 1980 with constant $d$; see the account in Ambrus-Heck 2025); $S(X, d) \leq d - 1 + 1/d$ for symmetric norms (Sevastyanov, confirming a claim of Banaszczyk; the AimPL page records this as 'Banaszczyk improved this to $d - 1/d$'); $S(\ell_1^d, d) \geq (d+1)/2$ (Grinberg-Sevastyanov), so the linear bound is tight up to a factor $2$ among symmetric norms, and it is exactly tight for asymmetric norms (regular simplex); $S(X, d) \geq \alpha(X, X, d)$ where $\alpha$ is the vector-balancing constant of Problem 1.5 (Chobanyan, as recorded on the AimPL page); the exact planar Euclidean constant was determined by Banaszczyk (1987). Conjecture (Euclidean Steinitz). $S(\ell_2^d, d) = O(\sqrt{d})$. Known: $\sqrt{d+3}/2 \leq S(\ell_2^d, d) \leq d - 1 + 1/d$, and $S_n(\ell_2^d, d) = O(\sqrt{d} + \sqrt{\log n})$ (Banaszczyk 2012, non-constructive), so the conjecture holds whenever $d \geq C\log n$. Algorithmic: $O(\sqrt{d \log n})$ (Bansal-Garg 2017; the workshop remark on the AimPL page records an algorithmic guarantee of $\sqrt{d}\log n$); $O(\sqrt{d})$ whenever $d \geq C\log^7 n$ (Dutta-Jha-Jiang 2026, via SDP-guided Brownian motion and affine spectral independence; extends to $\ell_2$ prefix discrepancy). Question ($\ell_\infty$ Steinitz). Is $S(\ell_\infty^d, d) = O(\sqrt{d})$? Known: $\Omega(\sqrt{d}) \leq S(\ell_\infty^d, d) \leq d - 1 + 1/d$ (the lower bound from $\ell_\infty$ vector balancing, Problem 1.5, via Chobanyan's inequality); Banaszczyk 2012 also gives an $n$-dependent bound in the $\ell_\infty$ case, matched algorithmically by Bansal-Garg 2017. The Euclidean results do not transfer directly, since $B_\infty^d \subseteq \sqrt{d}\, B_2^d$ only (they give $O(d + \sqrt{d \log n})$). Complete resolution. For $\ell_2$: a proof that $S(\ell_2^d, d) \leq C\sqrt{d}$ for all $d$ (independently of $n$) or a lower bound $S(\ell_2^d, d) = \omega(\sqrt{d})$; for $\ell_\infty$: the same with $\ell_\infty$; a polynomial-time algorithm achieving the same bounds resolves the constructive part. Minimal progress that counts as a solution of this record. Any of: (i) $S_n(\ell_2^d, d) = O(\sqrt{d} + g(n))$ with $g(n) = o(\sqrt{\log n})$, i.e. extending the range $d \geq C\log n$ in which Banaszczyk's bound gives $O(\sqrt{d})$ to $d \geq (\log n)^{1-\delta}$ for some $\delta > 0$; (ii) a polynomial-time algorithm achieving $O(\sqrt{d})$ for $\ell_2$ whenever $d \geq (\log n)^{\gamma}$ for some constant $\gamma < 7$ (improving Dutta-Jha-Jiang), or matching Banaszczyk's $O(\sqrt{d} + \sqrt{\log n})$ constructively for all $d, n$; (iii) for $\ell_\infty$: any bound $S_n(\ell_\infty^d, d) = O(d^{1-\delta}\,\mathrm{polylog}(n))$ with $\delta > 0$, or $O(\sqrt{d})$ in any regime $d \geq g(n)$ with $g$ polylogarithmic; (iv) a lower bound $S(\ell_2^d, d) = \omega(\sqrt{d})$ or $S(\ell_\infty^d, d) = \omega(\sqrt{d})$ (disproving the respective conjecture); (v) for general or symmetric norms, improving the dimension dependence $d$ (resp. $d - 1 + 1/d$) to $(1 - \delta) d$ for a universal $\delta > 0$, or proving this impossible. Improving constants or the exponent $7$ by less than one does not count.

comments.body: An algorithmic guarantee of $\sqrt{d}\log\,n$ was worked upon in the workshop.

literature.title: E. Steinitz, Bedingt konvergente Reihen und konvexe Systeme, Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik 143:128-176, 1913
literature.description: Origin of the Steinitz lemma: any zero-sum family of vectors in the unit ball of a $d$-dimensional normed space can be ordered with all partial sums of norm $\leq 2d$.

literature.title: V. S. Grinberg, S. V. Sevastyanov, Value of the Steinitz constant, Functional Analysis and Its Applications 14(2):125-126, 1980
literature.description: Proves $S(X, d) \leq d$ for every norm on $\mathbb{R}^d$ (sharpening Steinitz's $2d$) and exhibits the lower bound $S(\ell_1^d) \geq (d+1)/2$; Sevastyanov later sharpened the symmetric-norm bound to $d - 1 + 1/d$.

literature.title: W. Banaszczyk, On series of signed vectors and their rearrangements, Random Structures & Algorithms 40(3):301-316, 2012
literature.description: Proves $S_n(\ell_2^d, d) = O(\sqrt{d} + \sqrt{\log n})$ for the Euclidean Steinitz problem (non-constructively), matching the conjectured $O(\sqrt{d})$ when $d \geq \log n$.

literature.title: S. Chobanyan, Convergence a.s. of rearranged random series in Banach space and associated inequalities, in: Probability in Banach Spaces 9, Progress in Probability 35, Birkhäuser, 1994, pp. 3-29
literature.description: Relates the Steinitz constant to the vector-balancing constant ($S(X, d) \geq \alpha(X, X, d)$, as recorded on the AimPL page) and studies rearrangement inequalities for signed series.

literature.title: I. Bárány, On the power of linear dependencies, in: Building Bridges (M. Grötschel, G. O. H. Katona, eds.), Bolyai Society Mathematical Studies 19, Springer, 2008, pp. 31-45
literature.description: Survey of the Steinitz lemma and its applications, including the state of the Euclidean $O(\sqrt{d})$ conjecture.

literature.title: N. Bansal, S. Garg, Algorithmic discrepancy beyond partial coloring, STOC 2017; arXiv:1611.01805
literature.description: General algorithmic framework that overcomes the iterated-partial-coloring loss. For Tusnády's problem it improves the planar bound from $O(\log^{2.5} n)$ to $O(\log^2 n)$ and gives $O_d(\log^d n)$ for boxes in $\mathbb{R}^d$ (since improved to $O(\log^{d-1/2} n)$ by Nikolov). For the Steinitz problem it gives the first algorithm matching Banaszczyk's non-constructive $\ell_\infty$ bound and an algorithmic $O(\sqrt{d \log n})$ bound in the $\ell_2$ case.

literature.title: G. Ambrus, R. Heck, A note on the Steinitz lemma, arXiv:2505.09465, 2025
literature.description: Establishes the connection between the Steinitz problem for zero-sum families in arbitrary (possibly asymmetric) norms and its variant for nearly-unit families without the zero-sum condition; its introduction gives a careful account of the known bounds: $S(B) \leq d$ for every norm (Sevastyanov; Grinberg-Sevastyanov), $d - 1 + 1/d$ for symmetric norms (Sevastyanov), $S(B_1^d) \geq (d+1)/2$, $S(B_2^d) \geq \sqrt{d+3}/2$, and Banaszczyk's determination of the planar Euclidean constant.

literature.title: K. Dutta, A. V. Jha, H. Jiang, Near-optimal constructive bounds for $\ell_2$ prefix discrepancy and Steinitz problems via affine spectral independence, arXiv:2604.13355, 2026
literature.description: Efficient algorithm achieving the conjectured $O(\sqrt{d})$ bound for the $\ell_2$ Steinitz problem (and $\ell_2$ prefix discrepancy) whenever $d \geq \Omega(\log^7 n)$, using an SDP-guided discrete Brownian motion, the decoupling-via-affine-spectral-independence technique of Bansal-Jiang and a global interval-tree data structure; previous best algorithmic bound was $O(\sqrt{d \log n})$ (Bansal-Garg).

problems.statusDetails: General norms: $S(X, d) \leq d$ (Grinberg-Sevastyanov 1980, after Steinitz's $2d$), $d - 1 + 1/d$ for symmetric norms (Sevastyanov), tight up to a factor $2$ since $S(\ell_1^d, d) \geq (d+1)/2$.
